drills.title: 2v2 press and cover: keep them out of the target
drills.summary: Two defenders work as a pair, one pressing and one covering, to keep two attackers out of a target for eight seconds.
drills.setup: An area 18 m wide and 15 m deep, with a target 4 m wide and 2.5 m deep, marked with cones, in the middle of the end line. The target stands in for your penalty area. Two attackers start about 12 m from the target, two defenders between them and the target, and a server on the far line with the balls.
instructions: The server plays the ball to either attacker to start.
The attackers score by dribbling the ball into the target under control.
The defenders score by keeping the ball out of the target for 8 seconds; the coach counts.
Defenders may not stand in the target: they have to stop the ball before it gets there.
Each rep lasts 20 to 30 seconds, then reset. Keep the same defending pair for 4 or 5 reps, then rotate roles.
coaching_points: The nearer defender presses: close down while the ball travels, then arrive side-on and show the attacker wide, away from the target.
The other defender covers: stay between your own attacker and the target, close enough to step in if your partner is beaten.
When the ball is passed, swap jobs: the new nearest presses, the other drops in behind to cover.
Call "press" and "cover" out loud, so you both know who is doing what.
Be patient: keeping them out for the 8 seconds is the win, so don't lunge in.
Stop play now and then and ask: who's pressing, who's covering, and where should you be?

variations.title: Attackers at jogging pace
variations.change: The attackers may only dribble at jogging pace, and the defenders need to hold out for 10 seconds, so the pair has time to set up who presses and who covers.
instructions: The server plays the ball to either attacker to start.
The attackers dribble at jogging pace only, and score by dribbling into the target.
The defenders score by keeping the ball out of the target for 10 seconds.
Defenders may not stand in the target.
Keep the same defending pair for 4 or 5 reps, then rotate roles.

variations.title: 2v2: hold them out for 8 seconds
variations.change: Live 2v2: the defenders press and cover to keep the attackers out of a 4 m target for 8 seconds.

variations.title: Serve from anywhere
variations.change: The server plays from the left, the right or the middle, and from different distances, so the defenders can't set up before the ball arrives.
variations.setup: An area 18 m wide and 15 m deep, with a target 4 m wide and 2.5 m deep, marked with cones, in the middle of the end line. Two attackers start between 8 and 14 m from the target, anywhere across the area; two defenders between them and the target. The server moves along the far line and the sides between reps.

variations.title: 3v2 with a defender recovering
variations.change: A third attacker joins, and the target is 5 m wide. A third defender starts behind the play and sprints back, so the front two learn to delay until help arrives.
variations.setup: An area 18 m wide and 15 m deep, with a target 5 m wide and 2.5 m deep in the middle of the end line. Three attackers start about 12 m from the target, two defenders between them and the target, and a third defender behind the attackers, near the server.
instructions: The server plays the ball to an attacker; the third defender sprints back as soon as it's played.
The attackers score by dribbling the ball into the target.
The defenders score by keeping the ball out of the target for 8 seconds.
Defenders may not stand in the target.
Rotate roles every 4 or 5 reps.
coaching_points: Outnumbered, the presser delays: close down, then back off slowly and don't dive in.
The cover stays between the next attacker and the target, behind the presser.
The recovering defender sprints back goal-side on the shortest line, then picks up the free attacker.
Talk: the front two call "delay", the recovering defender calls who they're taking.

variations.title: 3v2, no help
variations.change: Three attackers against two defenders, with nobody coming back: the pair has to cover and talk while outnumbered.
variations.setup: An area 18 m wide and 15 m deep, with a target 5 m wide and 2.5 m deep in the middle of the end line. Three attackers start about 12 m from the target, two defenders between them and the target, and a server on the far line.
instructions: The server plays the ball to an attacker to start.
The attackers score by dribbling the ball into the target.
The defenders score by keeping the ball out of the target for 8 seconds; shorten it to 6 if the attackers win too easily.
Defenders may not stand in the target.
Rotate roles every 4 or 5 reps.
coaching_points: The presser delays and shows the attacker wide, away from the target and the other attackers.
The cover stays between the next most dangerous attacker and the target; the attacker furthest from the ball is left for now.
When the ball is passed, slide together: the new nearest presses, the other drops in to cover.
Keep talking: who's pressing, who's covering, and who's free.

media.caption: One defender presses and shows the attacker wide; the other covers, between their own attacker and the target

steps.label: The server plays to A2. D2, the nearer defender, presses; D1 drops between A1 and the target, close enough to cover D2
D2 arrives side-on and shows A2 wide, away from the target; D1 shifts across with them
A2 passes inside to A1. D1 steps out to press; D2 drops back inside to cover
D1 shows A1 wide; D2 stays between A2 and the target, and behind D1
Eight seconds and the ball is still out of the target: the defenders score

media.caption: Harder: 3v2 while a third defender recovers

steps.label: The server plays to A2 in the middle. D1 presses but doesn't dive in; D2 covers, between A3 and the target; D3 sprints back
D1 backs off slowly to delay while help arrives
A2 passes wide to A3. D2 slides out to press, D1 drops in to cover and D3 picks up A1
D2 shows A3 wide; D1 stays between A2 and the target and D3 stays goal-side of A1
The ball is kept out of the target until time is up: the defenders score
The server plays to A2 in the middle. D1 presses but doesn't dive in; D2 covers, between A3 and the target
D1 backs off slowly to delay: two against three, so time is the defenders' friend
A2 passes wide to A3. D2 slides out to press, D1 drops in to cover, and A1, furthest from the ball, is left for now
D2 shows A3 wide; D1 stays between A2 and the target, talking to D2
The ball is kept out of the target until time is up: the defenders score

drills.title: Move as a team with the ball
drills.summary: The coach moves the ball and the team adjusts its shape together, first unopposed, then around walking opponents.
drills.setup: Half of the pitch you play on, with cones at the corners. The players stand in the shape they play in for your formation, in the half nearest their goal. The coach stands in front of them with a ball. With more than 11, run two groups and let the resting group check the other's shape.
instructions: The coach carries the ball to a new spot, at a jog, and stops.
Every time the ball moves, every player moves: the nearest go towards it, the far side tucks in towards the middle.
When the ball stops, everyone stops. The coach checks the shape and asks one question, such as "who's closest to the ball, and is that right?"
After a few goes, the coach moves the ball without stopping, and the players keep adjusting.
coaching_points: The ball is your reference: watch it and your nearest teammates, not just the coach.
Keep about the same distance to your nearest teammates wherever the ball goes: close enough to pass to, not so close one opponent could mark you both.
Don't stand level with the teammate next to you: be a little in front or behind.
Near the ball, close together; far from the ball, tuck in towards the middle.
When the ball comes towards your goal, drop back and stay goal-side of it.
Keep the unopposed part short: once players know where to go, move on to the walking opponents, which is what they'll read in a game.

variations.title: Walk it through
variations.change: Everyone walks, and the coach stops after every move to check the shape and say where each player should be.

variations.title: The ball moves, everyone moves
variations.change: At a jog, with the coach stopping the ball now and then to check the shape.

variations.title: Ours or theirs
variations.change: As the coach moves the ball, they call "ours" or "theirs". On "ours", the team spreads out wide and deep to make the pitch big; on "theirs", it squeezes in around the ball and gets goal-side. Best with 7 or more players.
instructions: The coach carries the ball to a new spot and calls "ours" or "theirs".
"Ours": spread out, wide and deep, so there's space to pass into.
"Theirs": squeeze in around the ball and get goal-side of it.
Every time the ball moves, every player moves; the coach checks the shape now and then.

variations.title: Walking opponents
variations.change: Three or four opponents walk the ball around and pass it between them, without tackling. The team adjusts to the ball and stays goal-side of the opponents.
variations.setup: Half of the pitch you play on, with cones at the corners. The team stands in its shape in the half nearest its goal; three or four opponents in bibs stand in front of them with a ball.
instructions: The opponents walk with the ball and pass it between them. They don't tackle and nobody tackles them.
Every time the ball moves, the team moves: the nearest player steps up to the ball, the rest adjust and stay goal-side of the opponents.
The coach stops play now and then to check the shape.
Swap the opponents every few minutes.

media.caption: Every time the ball moves, every player moves. The shape shown (two lines of three) is only an example: use your team's own

steps.label: The coach carries the ball to the right. Everyone moves: the players nearest the ball close in, the far side tucks in towards the middle
The coach takes it across to the left. The whole shape slides with it, keeping the same distances
The coach drives at goal through the middle. The shape drops back and squeezes in, staying goal-side of the ball

media.caption: Harder: the team adjusts to walking opponents passing the ball

steps.label: The walking opponents pass to the right. The shape slides across while the ball travels
A long pass to the far side. Everyone shifts back across, and the player nearest the ball steps up to it
The opponent walks the ball towards goal: the nearest player stays in front, and the rest stay goal-side of their opponents

drills.title: Game in thirds: hold your area, then step out and back
drills.summary: A game on a pitch marked in thirds: players hold their area, then learn to step out and get back into shape when the ball is lost.
drills.setup: A pitch for the numbers you have, from about 30 x 40 m for 4v4 up to your full match pitch, with goals and goalkeepers. Mark two lines across it with cones to make three thirds. Give each player the third that matches their position in your formation, so each team has players in every third.
instructions: Play a normal game, but every player stays in their own third.
Restart from the goalkeeper after every goal and every ball out of play.
A player who leaves their third gives the ball to the other team.
Every few minutes, stop and move some players to a different third, so they learn other positions too.
coaching_points: Know your third, and where in it to be: move with the ball inside it.
When your team has the ball, spread out across your third so there's someone to pass to.
When the ball's lost, get goal-side quickly, and close in towards the ball.
Talk to the players in the next third: "drop", "push up", "I'm here".
Keep the lines for a short block: they help players learn where to be, but they also make players move less together. Take them away once players hold their positions.

variations.title: Two halves
variations.change: One line across the middle instead of two, so players only stay in their half: a back group and a front group.
variations.setup: A pitch for the numbers you have, from about 30 x 40 m for 4v4 up to your full match pitch, with goals and goalkeepers. Mark a line across the middle with cones. Give each player the half that matches their position, so each team has players in both halves.

variations.title: Stay in your third
variations.change: Three thirds, and every player stays in their own.

variations.title: One steps up, everyone gets back
variations.change: When a team has the ball, one player may move up into the next third. As soon as the ball is lost, they sprint back into their own.
instructions: Play a game with every player in their own third.
When your team has the ball, one player may move up into the next third.
As soon as the ball is lost, they sprint back into their own third. A goal scored while they're still out of it counts double.
Restart from the goalkeeper after every goal and every ball out of play.

variations.title: No lines: freeze
variations.change: Take the lines away and play freely. A few times a game, the coach calls "freeze": a team whose players are in their areas and at good distances from each other scores a point.
variations.setup: A pitch for the numbers you have, from about 30 x 40 m for 4v4 up to your full match pitch, with goals and goalkeepers. No lines: each player plays their usual position.
instructions: Play a normal game, with each player in their usual position.
A few times a game, the coach calls "freeze" and everyone stops where they are.
A team whose players are in their areas, at good distances from each other and goal-side when they haven't got the ball, scores a point.
Ask the players to put right anything that's out, then play on.

media.caption: Every player moves with the ball, inside their own third. The diagram shows 4v4 with goalkeepers; any numbers work

steps.label: The goalkeeper plays out to A1. Everyone moves with the ball, but stays inside their own third
A1 passes to A3. The red middle players shift across to the ball inside their third, and A4 moves away from B1
A3 plays forward to A4, who has found space inside the attacking third
A4 shoots

media.caption: Harder: one player steps up, and sprints back when the ball's lost

steps.label: A2 carries the ball up into the attacking third: one player may step up when their team has it
B1 wins the ball. A2 sprints straight back into the middle third; the others get goal-side
Red play forward, but blue are back in shape

drills.title: Slide together to protect the gates
drills.summary: A line of defenders shifts across together as the ball moves, to stop attackers dribbling through any of a row of small goals.
drills.setup: An area 30 m wide and about 22 m deep. Along the defenders' end line, put one more small goal (or 2 m cone gate) than there are defenders, spread evenly: five for a line of four. Mark a line 12 m out from the goals. A line of three to five defenders starts just inside it; the same number of attackers spread across the far end. The coach stands on the far line with the balls.
instructions: The coach plays the ball to an attacker.
The attackers pass it across the area and try to dribble through any goal. Each goal is a point.
The defenders score a point by winning the ball, or by keeping it out for 30 seconds.
Defenders may not stand in a goal: they have to stop the ball before it gets there.
Swap roles every three minutes.
coaching_points: The ball is your reference: every time it moves, the whole line moves, while it's travelling, not after it arrives.
The defender nearest the ball steps up to it; the next one covers just behind and inside.
The players nearest the ball stay closest together. The far side tucks in: leave the goal furthest from the ball, never the near one.
Keep about 5 to 7 m between neighbours, less with younger players.
Talk the whole time: "shift", "step", "drop", "I've got the ball".

variations.title: Passing slowly
variations.change: The attackers take two touches every time and may only try for a goal after four passes, so the line has time to shift.
instructions: The coach plays the ball to an attacker.
The attackers take two touches each and pass across the area. After four passes, they may try to dribble through any goal.
The defenders score a point by winning the ball, or by keeping it out for 30 seconds.
Defenders may not stand in a goal.
Swap roles every three minutes.

variations.title: Live
variations.change: Live: the attackers pass and dribble freely, and the line shifts to stop them.

variations.title: One more attacker
variations.change: The attackers have one more player than the defenders, so one is always free. The line has to stay close on the ball side and accept the far side is open.
variations.setup: An area 30 m wide and about 22 m deep. Along the defenders' end line, put one more small goal (or 2 m cone gate) than there are defenders, spread evenly: five for a line of four. Mark a line 12 m out from the goals. A line of three to five defenders starts just inside it; one more attacker than defenders spread across the far end. The coach stands on the far line with the balls.
coaching_points: Shift while the ball travels: a long switch is the moment the line has to move fastest.
The defender nearest the ball delays: stay in front and don't dive in.
Stay close together on the ball side. The free attacker is on the far side, and that's the one to leave.
Talk: the far defender tells the line when to shift.

media.caption: The line of four slides with the ball, closest on the ball side. Any number from three to five works, with one more goal than defenders

steps.label: The coach plays to A1. The line slides left while the ball travels: D1 steps up, D2 covers behind, the far side tucks in
A1 passes to A2. D2 steps up and D1 drops in behind
A2 passes to A3. The whole line shifts back across together
A3 passes wide to A4. D4 steps up; the gate furthest from the ball is the one left open
A4 tries to go inside; D4 blocks it and D3 is there behind, so A4 has to pass back

media.caption: Harder: five attackers against a line of four

steps.label: The coach plays to A2. The line slides towards the ball, and the far defender tucks in
A2 switches it to A5. The line slides across while the ball travels; D4 gets out in time to stop A5 running at the gate
With five attackers, one is always free: D4 delays and the others stay close to the ball side, leaving the far side
